faq.q: When do I use a capital letter?
faq.a: Use a capital at the start of every sentence, for names of people, places, days and months, and for the word I.

faq.q: Where does a full stop go?
faq.a: A full stop goes right after the last word of a sentence that tells something, with no space before it: We ate dumplings.
asks: How do I use a full stop?

faq.q: Does I need a capital letter?
faq.a: Yes, the word I is always a capital, wherever it is in the sentence.
asks: Why is I always a capital?

faq.q: Do days and months need capitals?
faq.a: Yes, in English days and months are names, so they take capitals: Monday, March. Seasons like summer do not.

faq.q: When do I use a question mark instead of a full stop?
faq.a: Use a question mark when the sentence asks something: Where is my bag? Use an exclamation mark for a shout or surprise: Watch out!

facts: Early Latin and Greek were often written in all capitals with no spaces or full stops.
In French and Spanish, days and months do not take capital letters.
